--- title: "Slide Decks" engine: knitr --- ## Your report is almost a deck In the terminal, copy your report: ```bash cp report.qmd slides.qmd ```
In `slides.qmd`, replace the `format:` lines with one line: ```yaml --- title: "Ice Cover on Lake Mendota" author: "Your Name" date: today format: revealjs --- ```
- [revealjs]{.uwred} is Quarto's format for slides in a web browser - Yes, this copies your code; the paper unit comes back to that
Render, then open `slides.html` in your browser: ```bash quarto render slides.qmd ``` - Use the arrow keys to move between slides -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## What you got You changed one line, and: - The YAML header made a [title slide]{.uwred} - Each `##` heading started a new slide - The code is gone: decks hide code by default
But one slide has a problem: - The figure shares its slide with your three sentences - Quarto shrinks the figure to make room for them -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## One idea per slide Add a heading just above your sentences: ```markdown ## The numbers Before 1900, the lake averaged `r mean_1800s` days of ice. Since 2000, it has averaged `r mean_recent`. ```
- The sentences move to a new slide - The figure now has its slide to itself, and it grows to fill it
Want a new slide [without]{.uwred} a title? - Put `---` on a line by itself, with blank lines around it -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Bullets and pauses Slides read better as short bullets than as sentences: ```markdown ## The numbers - Before 1900: `r mean_1800s` days of ice per winter - Since 2000: `r mean_recent` days . . . - Shortest winter: `r min(ice$ice_days)` days - Longest winter: `r max(ice$ice_days)` days ```
`. . .` on a line by itself is a [pause]{.uwred}. - The slide shows everything above it first - Press → to show the rest - Keep blank lines around it -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Speaker notes At the bottom of a slide, add: ```markdown ::: {.notes} About a month less ice than in the 1800s. ::: ```
- Everything between `::: {.notes}` and `:::` is a note - Your audience doesn't see notes
Press [S]{.uwred} for speaker view: - Your notes, a timer, and the next slide - If nothing opens, allow pop-ups for the page -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Your turn ::: {.callout-wide} ::: {.callout-important} # Try it 1. Add the `## The numbers` heading, render, and check that the figure has its own slide 2. Turn your sentences into bullets, with a `. . .` pause 3. Add a speaker note to one slide, render, and press S ::: ::: -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Optional: publish your deck First, give your deck its own title in the YAML header: ```yaml title: "Less Ice on Lake Mendota" ``` - Connect Cloud takes the title from your YAML, but only on the [first]{.uwred} publish - Your report already uses "Ice Cover on Lake Mendota"
Then publish, just like the report: ```bash quarto publish posit-connect-cloud slides.qmd ``` - The deck gets its own URL - `_publish.yml` adds a second entry, for `slides.qmd` -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Where we are We have: - Turned the report into a slide deck by changing `format:` - Split slides with `##` headings, so each idea gets its own slide - Added bullets, pauses, and speaker notes
::: {.callout-wide} ::: {.callout-important} # Next up A project often goes from report, to slides for a conference talk, to a [paper]{.uwred}. Next we will write the paper. ::: :::
